body:
## Context

ClarkCant already has a strong partial foundation for theming:

- `@clarkcant/design-tokens` exposes versioned semantic color/type/spacing/radius/motion/layout tokens and generates `--cc-*` CSS variables.
- `packages/conversation-client/src/theme.ts` supports `system | light | dark` and scopes appearance through `data-cc-theme`.
- Widget Lab can preview a subtree under a different theme.
- Generic package/install contracts already include a `themes` facet and correctly classify theme-only changes as UI refreshes rather than Pi-worker restarts.
- `DESIGN.md` already describes package themes/personalization as part of the target marketplace architecture.

However, the implementation still treats **theme == light/dark color scheme**. `ThemeName` is effectively `"dark" | "light"`, the widget-specific package reader only understands widget facets, desktop chrome still contains its own visual constants, and isolated iframe widgets receive no appearance information through the Widget SDK bridge.

The goal of this issue is to turn the existing partial theming work into a **first-class, marketplace-ready Theme Platform** that is expressive enough for visual systems such as Pixel Arcade, Neo Brutalism, Paper, Glass, Terminal, etc. — not merely palette/font swaps.

---

# Product decision

A ClarkCant theme is **not arbitrary global CSS or JavaScript**.

Marketplace themes must be declarative resources compiled by the host into a bounded, versioned appearance contract.

```text
Theme package
      │
      ▼
theme.json
      │
      ▼
Theme validator/compiler
      │
      ▼
AppearanceSnapshot
      │
      ├── Web host UI
      ├── Desktop shell
      ├── Built-in widgets
      ├── Declarative Mini Apps
      ├── Isolated iframe widgets
      ├── Detached widget windows
      └── Orb defaults
```

Do **not** allow third-party themes to inject unrestricted global CSS/JS into privileged ClarkCant chrome.

That would allow a theme to hide or spoof approval/credential/trust UI, depend on internal DOM/class names, issue network requests through CSS assets, or make Stop/focus/error states visually ambiguous.

Theme facets should default to the existing `declarative` isolation lane.

---

# Blockers / dependencies

## Hard blocker

- **Blocked by #198 — Widgets v2: universal composable catalog and multi-facet backend/service architecture**
  - Theme support should land on the canonical multi-facet package model rather than extending the current widget-only manifest reader.
  - Do not create a second theme-specific installer/package identity model.
  - The `themes` facet already exists in generic install contracts; #198 must converge authoring/runtime onto that canonical model.

## Phase/integration dependencies

- **#194 — Marketplace: npm-first widget distribution with separate discovery/curation site**
  - Blocks the final Marketplace browse/discovery/publish experience, but not the local Theme runtime/compiler.
  - Theme distribution should use the same npm/git/local package pipeline and DirectoryProvider abstraction.
- **#192 — Orb personalization**
  - Required for complete Theme → Orb default integration.
  - Theme may suggest/default an Orb profile/palette/effect, but explicit user Orb choices must win.
- **#129 — unified AppIntent control**
  - Required for conversational/voice theme operations such as “switch to Pixel Arcade” or “reset appearance”.
- **#200 — Widget platform expansion**
  - Coordinate package CLI/dev-host/conformance work so Theme developer tooling uses the same generalized package platform rather than creating parallel tooling.
- **#128 — Widget Library + Widget Lab** (closed)
  - Reuse its production-renderer preview philosophy and theme-preview mechanics as the foundation for a Theme Gallery / Theme Lab.

---

# Core architecture

## 1. Separate Theme from Color Scheme

Current semantics conflate:

```text
theme = system | light | dark
```

Target semantics:

```text
Theme
  Clark Default
  Pixel Arcade
  Neo Brutalism
  ...

Color scheme
  System
  Light
  Dark
```

Introduce preferences conceptually similar to:

```text
experience.themeRef
experience.colorScheme
experience.motion
experience.density
orb.profile
orb.custom
```

Migrate the current `experience.theme` value into `experience.colorScheme` without losing user preference.

Default:

```text
experience.themeRef = builtin:clark
experience.colorScheme = system
```

Do not silently reinterpret the old preference.

---

## 2. Add a versioned Theme contract

Add a dedicated contract, e.g.:

```text
packages/contracts/src/themes.ts
```

Target concepts:

- `ThemeRef`
- `ThemeDocument`
- `ColorScheme`
- `AppearanceSnapshot`
- `AppearanceContractVersion`
- theme assets
- semantic token groups
- component recipes
- motion/effect descriptors
- compatibility bounds

Do not expose `@clarkcant/design-tokens` package semver directly as the public Marketplace wire protocol.

Prefer independent versioning:

```text
hostApi
appearanceApi
tokenContractVersion
```

---

## 3. Theme document must be expressive beyond colors/fonts

A Theme should be able to define a bounded visual system across:

```text
Theme
├── color
├── typography
├── geometry
├── spacing / density
├── borders
├── shadows
├── motion
├── surfaces
├── controls
├── icon treatment
├── decorative effects
├── conversation treatment
├── widget treatment
├── window/chrome treatment
└── orb defaults
```

Example concepts:

### Neo Brutalism

- near-zero radii;
- heavy borders;
- hard offset shadows;
- raised/pressed button treatment;
- strong headings;
- flat surfaces;
- high-visibility focus treatment.

### Pixel Arcade

- zero/small radii;
- pixel display typography with readable body fallback;
- crisp borders;
- stepped/hard shadows;
- stepped/snap motion vocabulary;
- optional bounded scanline/pixel-grid effect;
- compatible Orb visual profile.

These should remain declarative.

---

## 4. Add host-owned Component Recipes

Tokens alone are not expressive enough for radically different themes.

Allow Theme documents to select from host-owned recipes, e.g.:

```json
{
  "recipes": {
    "button": "raised-hard",
    "input": "outlined",
    "card": "offset-shadow",
    "modal": "frame-heavy",
    "badge": "square",
    "composer": "floating-panel"
  }
}
```

The recipe implementation stays in ClarkCant.

A Theme selects a bounded visual treatment; it does not supply selectors or arbitrary executable styling.

Possible initial recipe vocabulary:

- button: quiet / flat / outlined / raised-soft / raised-hard / beveled;
- card: flat / outlined / elevated-soft / offset-shadow;
- input: quiet / filled / outlined / hard-outline;
- modal: floating / framed / hard-frame;
- badge: pill / rounded / square;
- composer: integrated / floating / framed.

Keep this vocabulary versioned and extensible.

---

## 5. Add bounded decorative effect primitives

Support optional declarative effects such as:

- grain;
- scanlines;
- dot grid;
- hard grid;
- soft glow;
- glass;
- paper texture.

Example:

```json
{
  "effects": {
    "surface": {
      "kind": "scanlines",
      "intensity": 0.06,
      "scale": 2
    }
  }
}
```

Do not accept arbitrary shader code or arbitrary CSS.

Orb/shader customization remains behind its own bounded Orb contract.

---

# Package model

## 6. Theme as a normal package facet

Target manifest shape:

```json
{
  "id": "@community/pixel-arcade",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "facets": [
    {
      "kind": "themes",
      "entry": "themes/pixel-arcade/theme.json",
      "isolation": "declarative"
    }
  ]
}
```

A package may contain multiple facets:

```text
Weather Pack
├── ui
├── service
├── skills
└── themes
```

Install/risk behavior must continue using the strongest facet lane for the package.

Theme-only updates should hot-refresh UI without restarting Pi.

Use the existing package install/update/remove/rollback lifecycle.

---

## 7. Theme registry / compiler

Introduce a host-owned Theme Registry / Appearance Manager.

Responsibilities:

- discover active installed theme facets;
- validate theme schema;
- validate asset references;
- resolve compatibility;
- compile selected Theme + scheme + user overrides into an immutable/bounded `AppearanceSnapshot`;
- assign an appearance revision;
- provide fallback to `builtin:clark`;
- hot-swap on install/update/preference change;
- never expose unvalidated theme input directly to privileged UI.

Conceptual resolution order:

```text
Clark base appearance
        ↓
selected Theme facet
        ↓
resolved light/dark scheme
        ↓
explicit user personalization
        ↓
widget-instance limited overrides
        ↓
runtime interaction state
        ↓
mandatory accessibility / safety overrides
```

Explicit user choices must beat theme defaults.

---

# Host UI migration

## 8. Generalize design tokens

Refactor `packages/design-tokens` from static `DARK/LIGHT` data into:

- built-in Clark theme;
- public appearance token schema;
- theme compiler helpers;
- dynamic contrast/accessibility auditor;
- CSS variable emitter from an `AppearanceSnapshot`.

Keep the current Clark Default visually stable during the migration.

---

## 9. Tokenize remaining identity-level hard-coded styling

Audit and migrate visual identity constants still hard-coded in:

- `packages/conversation-client/src/styles/*`;
- conversation components;
- terminal appearance;
- `apps/desktop/src/shell.css`;
- other host-owned surfaces.

Prioritize identity-relevant values:

- radius;
- border width/style;
- shadows;
- typography;
- surface treatment;
- motion/easing;
- decorative effects;
- icon treatment.

Do not mechanically convert every numeric layout value into a theme token.

Layout/accessibility/product invariants may remain host-owned where allowing arbitrary changes would break usability.

---

## 10. Desktop/Web parity

The desktop shell must consume the same resolved appearance contract rather than maintaining a separate fixed palette.

Theme switching must stay consistent across:

- browser app;
- Electron desktop;
- normal/expanded/compact/orb window modes;
- detached widget windows.

No second desktop theme system.

---

# Widget / Mini App theming

## 11. Built-in catalog widgets

Built-in/declarative widgets should consume semantic appearance tokens/recipes and automatically adapt to the active Theme.

Mini App composition specs should stay semantic, e.g.:

```json
{
  "tone": "surface",
  "emphasis": "normal"
}
```

Do not embed fixed CSS values such as `#fff` or `12px` in declarative composition specs unless they are truly content data.

---

## 12. Add AppearanceSnapshot to the isolated Widget bridge

Current isolated iframe widgets do not inherit host CSS variables and currently receive no theme data.

Extend the host → widget bridge:

```text
init
  appearance: AppearanceSnapshot

appearance.changed
  revision
  appearance: AppearanceSnapshot
```

Changing theme must update a live iframe without remounting it.

Do not expose raw Theme package files to the iframe; send only the normalized public appearance contract.

---

## 13. Add Widget SDK appearance API

Add author-facing APIs conceptually like:

```ts
clark.appearance.current()
clark.appearance.subscribe(snapshot => {})
```

Provide an optional DOM adapter/helper that maps the bounded snapshot to `--cc-*` variables for ordinary web widgets.

Prefer keeping the core runtime DOM-independent and exposing DOM helpers from a separate subpath/module.

---

## 14. Widget appearance modes

Allow widget definitions/packages to declare an appearance behavior, e.g.:

```text
adaptive
fixed
```

- `adaptive` should be the recommended/default mode.
- `fixed` is allowed for strongly branded apps but Marketplace/Widget Lab should disclose that the widget uses its own visual system.

A fixed widget still cannot alter host chrome.

---

## 15. Historical snapshots

Changing the global Theme must not mutate historical data/content semantics, but historical widget/message presentation should generally render under the current appearance.

Keep immutable:

- message/content data;
- widget props/state captured for history;
- renderer/package provenance;
- fallback text.

Resolve appearance at render time.

Do not freeze an entire theme stylesheet into every historical presentation bundle.

---

## 16. Detached widgets

Detached widgets must receive the same host-owned appearance revision/snapshot through their existing host relay.

Do not give detached iframe code direct access to runtime credentials or a separate theme query path.

---

# Orb integration

## 17. Theme may provide Orb defaults, not authority

Theme may provide:

- preferred Orb profile;
- palette defaults;
- optical/effect defaults;
- compatible motion personality.

Precedence:

```text
explicit user Orb choice
    >
Theme Orb default
    >
Clark built-in default
```

A Theme must not remove/hide the Orb or replace Clark's identity with arbitrary executable content.

Respect #192 and the current product invariant that the Orb remains ClarkCant's signature identity.

Reduced-motion requirements always override theme animation preferences.

---

# Assets

## 18. Safe packaged theme assets

Allow bounded package-local assets where needed:

- fonts;
- raster textures/images;
- bounded icon resources.

Requirements:

- installed package-relative references only;
- immutable/digest-covered;
- MIME allowlist;
- size quotas;
- no remote CSS `url(...)` fetches;
- no path traversal;
- no arbitrary external fonts;
- define SVG policy explicitly; sanitize tightly or defer arbitrary SVG support initially.

Marketplace/conformance should expose license/source metadata where relevant.

---

# Security and accessibility invariants

## 19. Protected host semantics

A theme may visually restyle privileged host UI but must not erase its semantic distinctions.

Mandatory invariants include:

- Stop remains visible/actionable;
- approval/refusal states remain distinguishable;
- credential/trust chrome remains host-owned;
- danger/warning/success states remain distinguishable;
- focus remains visible;
- disabled controls remain recognizable;
- provenance/risk information remains legible;
- state is not communicated only by color.

Theme schema/compiler/conformance should reject invalid combinations instead of silently trusting package values.

---

## 20. Theme conformance

Generalize existing design-token audits to arbitrary Theme documents.

Minimum checks:

- [ ] primary text contrast;
- [ ] muted/tertiary text contrast where used as text;
- [ ] focus visibility;
- [ ] status semantics;
- [ ] required component boundary visibility;
- [ ] reduced-motion path;
- [ ] readable typography bounds;
- [ ] theme asset validation;
- [ ] no forbidden external/remote styling resources;
- [ ] no executable payload;
- [ ] protected host semantics remain usable;
- [ ] narrow/normal desktop journey remains usable.

Reduced motion must always win over Theme motion choices.

---

# Settings / UX

## 21. Experience settings

Keep Settings as a secondary surface; do not add a permanent top-level Themes page.

Target:

```text
Settings → Experience

Theme
  Clark Default                         >
  Recently used / installed
  [ Browse themes ]

Color scheme
  [ System | Light | Dark ]

Customize
  Accent
  Density
  Motion
  Orb

Reset theme customization
```

Selecting a Theme should apply immediately when safe and persist using the preference registry.

Opening Theme Gallery must preserve conversation state/focus just like current Settings/Widget Library behavior.

---

## 22. AppIntent / agent / voice integration

Once #129 provides the unified path, add bounded intents such as:

```text
appearance.set-theme
appearance.set-color-scheme
appearance.reset
appearance.open-theme-gallery
```

Examples:

- “use Pixel Arcade”
- “switch back to Clark Default”
- “follow system colors”
- “reset my appearance”
- “open themes”

Text, voice and click must converge on the same intent/action implementation.

---

# Theme Gallery / Theme Lab

## 23. Reuse the Widget Lab philosophy

Create a Theme Gallery / Theme Lab as a utility surface, not a new permanent navigation concept.

Theme Lab must render **real ClarkCant production components**, not screenshots or hand-built mocks.

Preview matrix should include:

- conversation;
- composer;
- buttons/inputs;
- cards/widgets;
- Settings/modal;
- approval/error/status states;
- Orb;
- compact/narrow viewport;
- light/dark scheme;
- reduced motion.

A Theme that only looks correct on a decorative cover image is not conformant.

---

# Developer experience

## 24. Theme tooling

Extend the generalized package CLI after #198/#200 convergence.

Target author flow:

```bash
clark theme init
clark theme dev
clark theme test
clark theme pack
```

Publishing remains npm-first per #194.

Theme dev host should provide:

- hot reload;
- production-component preview;
- scheme switch;
- viewport switch;
- reduced-motion switch;
- token inspector;
- recipe inspector;
- contrast/a11y results;
- asset validation;
- package manifest validation.

Do not create a separate package/install lifecycle just for themes.

---

# Marketplace integration

## 25. Theme discovery

Use the same Marketplace/DirectoryProvider architecture from #194.

Marketplace can expose/filter:

```text
facet: themes
```

Theme package detail should show:

- preview media;
- publisher/source/version;
- compatible Clark/appearance API versions;
- included facets;
- whether it is declarative-only;
- supported light/dark schemes;
- fonts/assets;
- accessibility/conformance status where available.

Installation must still route through ClarkCant's existing verified package installer.

Marketplace metadata is discovery information, not runtime authority.

---

# Reference themes

## 26. Ship reference themes proving the architecture

### `builtin:clark`

Must preserve the current visual baseline.

### Pixel Arcade

Must prove:

- packaged font or font-family profile;
- radically different geometry;
- hard/stepped borders and shadows;
- component recipes;
- bounded decorative effect;
- motion variation;
- themed Orb defaults;
- built-in + isolated widget adaptation.

### Neo Brutalism

Must prove:

- near-zero radius;
- heavy borders;
- hard offset shadows;
- strong type;
- pressed-state treatment;
- modal/card/control recipe differences;
- accessibility still passes.

If both Pixel Arcade and Neo Brutalism can be implemented without privileged/raw CSS escape hatches, the appearance contract is sufficiently expressive for V1.

---

# Suggested implementation phases

## M1 — Contract + preference split

- [ ] Theme/appearance contracts.
- [ ] `ThemeRef` vs `ColorScheme`.
- [ ] migrate current `experience.theme`.
- [ ] preserve Clark Default exactly.
- [ ] dynamic token/compiler foundation.

## M2 — Theme facet runtime

- [ ] canonical `themes` facet on generalized package manifest.
- [ ] Theme Registry.
- [ ] install/update/remove/rollback.
- [ ] hot UI activation.
- [ ] invalid/missing Theme fallback.

## M3 — Host appearance depth

- [ ] identity-level tokenization pass.
- [ ] component recipes.
- [ ] bounded visual effects.
- [ ] desktop parity.
- [ ] protected-host semantic rules.

## M4 — Widget appearance bridge

- [ ] `AppearanceSnapshot` in init.
- [ ] live `appearance.changed`.
- [ ] Widget SDK API.
- [ ] DOM adapter.
- [ ] built-in/declarative/iframe/detached parity.
- [ ] widget adaptive/fixed declaration.

## M5 — Theme developer tooling

- [ ] Theme Lab.
- [ ] CLI init/dev/test/pack.
- [ ] conformance/a11y/asset validation.
- [ ] live production-component preview.

## M6 — Marketplace integration

- [ ] Marketplace facet filtering.
- [ ] Theme detail/gallery UX.
- [ ] npm-first discovery/install.
- [ ] AppIntent/voice integration after #129.

## M7 — Reference themes

- [ ] Pixel Arcade.
- [ ] Neo Brutalism.
- [ ] cross-platform visual/E2E coverage.

---

# Tests / acceptance criteria

## Package/runtime

- [ ] A declarative Theme package installs through the canonical package lifecycle.
- [ ] Theme-only update refreshes UI without restarting Pi.
- [ ] Removing an active Theme falls back safely to Clark Default.
- [ ] Package digest/version/provenance remains visible.
- [ ] A package containing Theme + stronger facets is labeled by the strongest risk lane.

## Host UI

- [ ] Theme applies consistently to web and desktop.
- [ ] Theme changes do not reset conversation/composer/pinned widgets/voice state.
- [ ] System/light/dark resolution remains independent from selected Theme.
- [ ] Explicit user appearance/Orb overrides beat Theme defaults.
- [ ] reduced-motion always wins.

## Widgets

- [ ] Built-in widgets adapt to active Theme.
- [ ] Declarative Mini Apps adapt without embedding fixed visual constants.
- [ ] Isolated iframe receives initial appearance snapshot.
- [ ] Theme switching updates iframe without remount.
- [ ] Detached widget receives the same appearance revision.
- [ ] Fixed-appearance widgets are clearly identified.
- [ ] Theme changes do not create semantic-state/model-turn churn.

## Security

- [ ] Theme cannot inject arbitrary JS.
- [ ] Theme cannot inject arbitrary global CSS selectors.
- [ ] Theme cannot hide/spoof privileged approval/credential/trust chrome.
- [ ] Theme assets cannot escape package root or trigger undeclared remote fetches.
- [ ] protected interaction/status/focus semantics remain visible.

## Accessibility

- [ ] Contrast/conformance tests run against third-party Theme documents.
- [ ] keyboard-only flows still work.
- [ ] focus visibility is preserved.
- [ ] narrow and normal desktop widths remain usable.
- [ ] reduced motion has an equivalent path.

## Developer UX

- [ ] Developer can initialize, preview, test and pack a Theme without understanding runtime internals.
- [ ] Theme Lab uses production ClarkCant components.
- [ ] Pixel Arcade and Neo Brutalism both pass conformance without raw CSS/JS escape hatches.

---

# Definition of done

A community developer can create a visually distinctive ClarkCant Theme, test it locally, publish the package through the same npm-first ecosystem as other Clark packages, and have a user install/select it without granting executable authority.

The selected Theme consistently affects ClarkCant host UI, built-in widgets, declarative Mini Apps, isolated iframe widgets, detached windows and compatible Orb defaults while preserving:

- one-conversation UX;
- Clark's Orb identity;
- accessibility;
- reduced-motion behavior;
- trusted host chrome;
- package provenance;
- cross-platform compatibility;
- widget sandbox boundaries.

The architecture must be expressive enough for **Pixel Arcade** and **Neo Brutalism** without allowing unrestricted third-party global CSS or JavaScript.
